notes.envelope: This is the opening screen: keep the greeting short, then use the invitation message for the formal wording and how guests should address you.
notes.couple: Use the full names exactly as you want them printed. Short names are used on the envelope and smaller sections; leave them empty and they are taken from the full names. Leave "Birth order" blank and the card shows "Groom" / "Bride".
notes.families: Add both parents' names and each family's address. This is especially useful when a family-altar ceremony is held at home.
notes.ceremonies: Common ceremonies are the engagement, bride's family and groom's family ceremonies. Customs vary by region, so add only the ceremonies your families are actually holding.
notes.reception: Wedding venues often have separate guest-arrival and reception-start times. Include the full venue address; use Google Maps' Share button for the map link.
notes.dressCode: A dress-code hint for guests: describe it in a line or two, then pick colours from the suggestions or paste your own hex codes. Turn this block off if your wedding has no dress code.
notes.timeline: Order the day's milestones, such as guest arrival → ceremony → reception → photos. Add a start time for each activity so guests can follow the schedule easily; the end time is optional. Icons are drawn in the style of the selected template; on Auto, the icon follows the activity you type.
notes.countdown: Choose the ceremony or reception start time you want the countdown to target. It does not have to be the same as guest arrival.
notes.story: A few lines about the two of you — how you met, what made you choose each other. Three to five sentences reads best; this block sits right before the photo album.
notes.music: Choose one gentle background track; guests can turn it off when they open the invitation.
notes.thankYou: This message appears at the end of the invitation after guests have viewed the content.
notes.qrAuto: The bank transfer QR code is generated automatically from the account details.
notes.photoSlots: This template lays out {count} photo frames at fixed ratios — you fill them in; you cannot add frames or move them. Switching templates keeps your photos.
notes.noPhotoSlots: This template has no photo frames — it uses illustrations drawn for it. To put your real wedding photos on the card, pick a template with photo frames; everything you typed is kept.
notes.album: The album is included with every invitation and can be added to any template. It is separate from the photo frames each template lays out.
notes.wishes: Guests write their wishes right on the card. Every wish starts as pending — only the ones you approve appear on the card.
notes.rsvp: Guests confirm whether they're coming and how many, from any link. Only you can see this list. Personal links fill in the name, and sending again updates the earlier answer.

meta.title: How to create an online wedding invitation
meta.description: Find where each invitation editor field appears, with numbered screenshots from a real Burgundy Red invitation, then learn how to create and share your card.

guide.title: See where every field appears.

choose.title: Choose a template
choose.body: Explore 60+ templates and try a working invitation before choosing the style for your wedding.

instructions.title: Find your style
instructions.body: Open Templates to see reference designs, or message Keemori to have one designed to order.

instructions.title: Open the live preview
instructions.body: Open a template’s details and preview. Scroll through the envelope, photos, ceremony and reception sections on both a phone and a computer.

instructions.title: Check the photos
instructions.body: Each template lays out its own photo frames. The photo album is included with every invitation and can be added to any template.

instructions.title: Start editing
instructions.body: Select Use this template to open the editor. You can enter your content and preview it before signing in.

choose.hint: Choose a layout you like: fonts, colors and composition are designed as part of each template.
choose.caption: The real Keemori catalog: search, filter and preview designs.

content.title: Add your details and preview
content.body: Enter your wedding details, add photos and review each section before creating a link for your guests.

instructions.title: Couple and family details
instructions.body: Enter the couple’s full names and optional nicknames for the envelope. Check parents’ names and how each family is addressed.

instructions.title: Separate ceremony and reception details
instructions.body: Enter the date, time and place for each ceremony and the reception in their own sections. Check the reception Directions button and review every ceremony separately.

instructions.title: Add photos to the right slots
instructions.body: Choose cover and couple photos for the template’s slots. Photos upload as soon as you pick them, even before you sign in. Add a photo album if you like. Preview to check that faces are not cropped and text stays readable.

instructions.title: Complete optional sections
instructions.body: Add your story, timeline, music, thank-you message or gift details as needed. Use each section’s switch to hide anything you do not want to show.

instructions.title: Review the invitation
instructions.body: Open Preview and check phone and desktop layouts. Review spelling, dates, photos, music and maps. If you used sample data, replace all example details before sharing.

content.hint: Select Save & Create link to save your content. Keep the editor open until uploads and saving have finished.
content.caption: The editor for Hoàng Phong & Tú Linh’s Burgundy Red invitation.

share.title: Save and share your link or QR code
share.body: After saving, your invitation appears in My invitations with its own link for guests.

instructions.title: Save & Create link
instructions.body: Select Save & Create link. If you are signed out, sign in and return to finish saving. The content you just entered is kept for this step.

instructions.title: Check the status
instructions.body: In My invitations, check the invitation's status: draft or published. A published invitation has a permanent link with no view limit.

instructions.title: Copy the link or download the QR code
instructions.body: Open Link & QR, then select Copy to share through Zalo, Messenger or email. Download the QR code as a PNG for printed invitations or your welcome sign.

instructions.title: Test as a guest
instructions.body: Open the link on a phone and scan the QR code with the camera. Check the names, event details and map links before sending it to everyone.

instructions.title: Update after sharing
instructions.body: Go to My invitations, edit that invitation and save your changes. Keep its URL unchanged so guests can see updates through the same link. If you change the URL, download the new QR code and send the new link.

share.hint: The image shows an example link and QR code. Always share the link and QR code from your own invitation.
share.caption: The real sharing dialog: copy a link, open the invitation and download its QR code. Example data only.

6.body: One guest per line. “Cô Lan” appears on the opening screen of her personal link. The editor preview uses the first guest. Save, then copy each link from My invitations → Guest links.

7.label: Groom’s full name
7.body: Enter the full name. Burgundy Red uses the nickname (9) on its cover; if that is blank, it derives a short name from this field. This design has no separate full-name line.

8.label: Bride’s full name
8.body: Enter the full name. The cover uses the nickname (10), or derives a short name from this field when the nickname is blank.

9.label: Groom’s nickname
9.body: “Hoàng Phong” is the first large name on the cover, repeated on the envelope card, announcement and closing.

10.label: Bride’s nickname
10.body: “Tú Linh” is the large name below the ampersand on the cover and is repeated elsewhere in this design.

11.label: Groom’s birth order
11.body: For example, eldest son or second son. Burgundy Red does not display this field. It is kept for designs that show birth order.

12.label: Bride’s birth order
12.body: For example, eldest daughter or second daughter. This design does not display the field, so there is no marker 12 on the invitation.

13.label: Groom’s father
13.body: Appears after “Ông” in the groom’s family column. Enter the name without adding the title.

14.label: Groom’s mother
14.body: Appears after “Bà”, below the father’s name in the groom’s family column.

15.label: Groom’s family address
15.body: Appears below his parents’ names. This is the family address and does not replace the reception address.

16.label: Bride’s father
16.body: Appears after “Ông” in the bride’s family column.

17.label: Bride’s mother
17.body: Appears after “Bà”, below the father’s name in the bride’s family column.

18.label: Bride’s family address
18.body: Appears below her parents’ names. Include the street number, street and area.

19.label: Ceremony type
19.body: Sets the heading, such as “Lễ ăn hỏi”. Choosing another type reveals a custom-name field. Each added ceremony creates a similar entry.

20.label: Ceremony date
20.body: The date appears after the time below the ceremony heading. Each ceremony can have a different date.

21.label: Ceremony time
21.body: Hours and minutes become “08:00” at the start of the date/time line. Set each ceremony’s own time.

22.label: Ceremony venue
22.body: Appears directly below that ceremony’s date and time. Type an address or select a suggestion from the family addresses.

23.label: Ceremony note
23.body: Appears in italics below the venue, for example an invitation for close relatives to attend.

24.label: Reception date
24.body: Creates the large day number and month/year line. The weekday and lunar date are calculated automatically; the date is also repeated on the cover.

25.label: Guest arrival time
25.body: Appears in the “Đón khách: 17:30” line, separately from the reception start time.

26.label: Reception start time
26.body: Appears in the “Vào lúc 18:30, Chủ Nhật” line. This is when the reception starts.

27.label: Lead-in
27.body: The line directly above the reception venue address. Leave it blank to use the template’s default wording, or write your own introduction.

28.label: Reception venue address
28.body: The venue name and address appear above Directions. Include both the venue name and full address.

29.label: Google Maps link
29.body: Powers the Directions button; the raw URL is not printed. Paste a Maps sharing link and check the destination before sharing.

30.label: Dress code title
30.body: Sets the heading above the color palette.

31.label: Outfit description
31.body: Appears below the palette, describing the suggested outfits or colors.

32.label: Colors
32.body: Selected colors become swatches on the invitation. Suggested colors, the color picker and custom hex values all update this palette, up to six colors.

33.label: Timeline title
33.body: Appears above the schedule, such as “Lịch trình buổi lễ”.

34.label: Start time
34.body: Appears above the activity, such as 09:00 for the ceremony. Each activity has its own entry.

35.label: End time
35.body: Optional. It is blank in this saved invitation, so only the start time (33) appears. When filled, the line reads like “09:00 – 10:00”.

36.label: Activity icon
36.body: Burgundy Red uses fixed dots, so this choice does not change its symbols. Designs with activity icons use the selected activity type.

37.label: Activity
37.body: The activity name appears below its time, such as ceremony, welcome or reception.

38.label: Countdown date
38.body: Marks the wedding date on the calendar. This is a separate countdown/calendar setting; check that it agrees with your reception date.

39.label: Countdown time
39.body: Together with date 37, sets the countdown target and calendar event start. The remaining days, hours, minutes and seconds change over time.

40.label: Your story
40.body: Appears below the story heading and above the stationery photographs.

41.label: Wedding album
41.body: Uploaded photos appear in a horizontal album. Tap to enlarge. This is separate from the design photo slots.

42.label: Groom’s bank
42.body: Appears after opening the Groom envelope and is used to generate its transfer QR code.

43.label: Groom’s account number
43.body: Appears under the account-number label and is encoded in the QR. The pictured number is an example.

44.label: Groom’s account holder
44.body: Appears below the bank name. Enter the account holder’s correct name.

45.label: Bride’s bank
45.body: Appears in the Bride envelope’s dialog and is used for its QR code.

46.label: Bride’s account number
46.body: Appears in the Bride dialog. Check this account separately before sharing.

47.label: Bride’s account holder
47.body: Appears below the bank name in the Bride dialog.

48.label: Guestbook
48.body: Enables the guest wish form. The editor list is for moderation; only approved wishes appear publicly. This preview shows the form’s position.

49.label: RSVP
49.body: Enables the guest name, attendance and party-size form. Response lists and totals in the editor are private to the owner.

50.label: Background music
50.body: The track plays through the floating round button. Its title is not printed on the invitation. Guests can toggle playback; browsers may require a tap first.

51.label: Thank-you message
51.body: Appears below “Thank you” at the end of the invitation.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.subtitle: These terms apply to Keemori's made-to-order online event invitation design service (custom invitations). By ordering a design, paying, or signing in to the account we create for you, you agree to the terms below.

sections.heading: 1. Acceptance of terms
body: By ordering a design, paying, or signing in to a Keemori account, you confirm that you have read, understood and agree to be bound by these terms.
We record your acceptance together with the version of this document at that time. The version number is shown at the top of this page, and you can request an export of your own acceptance history.
If you do not agree with any part of these terms, please do not order a design and stop using the service.

sections.heading: 2. The service
body: Keemori designs online invitations to order for your event — birthdays, store openings, conferences, parties and other events. Each invitation is designed from scratch for one event, not picked from a ready-made template library.
An invitation is a web page with its own link and QR code, which you send to your guests by message, on social media or printed on paper.
The scope of each design — content, style, information blocks and included features — is agreed between us during the consultation, before you pay.
There is no trial. We only start designing once we have received full payment.

sections.heading: 3. How ordering works
body: You contact us through the channels on our Contact page and describe your event and what you want. We advise you and send a quote.
Once we agree on the brief, you pay the full order value by bank transfer. We start designing once the payment arrives.
We create a Keemori account for you, place the invitation in it and send you the sign-in details so you can review the design.
You send feedback through the channel we are using, and we make revisions as agreed during the consultation. The invitation is published once you confirm the final version.
Turnaround depends on the complexity of the design and how quickly both sides respond; we give you an estimated timeline during the consultation.

sections.heading: 4. Your account
body: Your account is created by us using the email address you provide. Change the password the first time you sign in; from then on you are responsible for keeping it secure.
You can also sign in with a Google or Facebook account that uses the same email address.
All activity under your account is treated as yours. Tell us immediately if you suspect unauthorised access.

In your account you can edit the text of your invitation yourself: event details, time, venue and invitation wording. The layout, fonts, colours and design work done by Keemori cannot be changed from your account — contact us if you want them changed.

sections.heading: 5. Price and payment
body: Prices are listed on the Pricing page, in Vietnamese đồng. The price of an order is fixed when you create the payment order, including any promotion or voucher code applied at that moment.
You pay 100% of the order value by bank transfer (VietQR) right on the website. The invitation's public link is only created once the money has arrived.
Payments are non-refundable, except where the invitation has a technical fault caused by Keemori.
Details on the payment process, handling of incorrect transfers and refunds are in our Payment & Refund Policy.

sections.heading: 6. Invitation links and duration
body: A paid invitation does not expire and has no limit on the number of viewers, for as long as your account exists.
Every invitation has a public link. Anyone with the link can view the invitation; we do not password-protect individual invitations.
A link that has been issued to your invitation will never be reissued to someone else's invitation.

Each invitation is designed for one event and must not be reused for another event by replacing its details. 15 days after the first successful payment, the host name shown on the invitation can no longer be edited from your account; contact support if it needs to change.

sections.heading: 7. Your content
body: You keep all rights to the content you provide: names, photos, logos, invitation wording and event details.
You grant us the right to store, process and display that content to the extent needed to design your invitation and run the service — for example, showing the invitation to people who open the link.
You are responsible for the lawfulness of your content, including the right to use any photos, logos, brands and other people's information you give us.
If your invitation has a guestbook, guests' wishes only appear after you approve them, and you can delete any wish at any time. You decide what appears on your invitation.

sections.heading: 8. Prohibited content
body: Do not post content that is unlawful, infringes the rights of others, or is fraudulent, harassing or hateful.
Do not use the service to spread malware or spam, or to collect other people's data without authorisation.
Do not attempt to probe, interfere with or disrupt the system.
We may decline to design content that breaches these rules.

sections.heading: 9. Intellectual property
body: The source code, platform and Keemori brand belong to us or our licensors.
The design made for you may be used for the event named in your order, as an online invitation on the Keemori platform. You may not copy, resell or use that design as a template for third parties.

sections.heading: 10. Suspension and termination
body: We may suspend or terminate accounts that breach these terms, and will give notice beforehand where possible.

You may stop using the service at any time. If you delete your own account, your account data is permanently deleted, the invitation links tied to it stop working, and amounts already paid are not refunded.
Accounts we disable for a breach lose sign-in access, but their data is kept for reconciliation — see the Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 11. Limitation of liability
body: The service is provided as is. We work to keep the system stable but do not promise it will never be interrupted.
To the extent permitted by law, our liability for any single incident does not exceed the amount you paid for the invitation concerned.
This limit does not apply to liability that cannot be excluded by law.

sections.heading: 12. Changes to these terms
body: These terms may be updated as the service changes. The version and date of the latest update are always shown at the top of this page.
If a change significantly affects your rights, we will notify you by email or within the product before it applies, and may ask you to accept the new version.

sections.heading: 13. Complaints and dispute resolution
body: Any complaint about the service — quality, payment, personal data or content on the platform — can be sent by support email or Facebook Messenger. Every complaint is recorded, even when the outcome is that we cannot do what you asked.
To help us act quickly, a complaint should include:
- The email of the account concerned.
- The invitation link or order code, if any.
- A description of what happened and when.
- The outcome you would like.
For payment complaints, please include the time of the transfer and the amount — those two details are enough for us to find the payment in our ledger.

We reply through the same channel you used, stating our conclusion and the reasons for it. If you are not satisfied, you may ask us to review it once more with additional information or arguments. We handle complaints as quickly as possible and reply within 3 working days of receiving them. If the matter needs to be verified with a third party — a bank or payment provider — and cannot be concluded within that time, we still reply within 3 working days to explain the status and when we expect to conclude.

Both parties will try to resolve disputes by negotiation first. If no agreement is reached, you may complain to the competent consumer protection authority or bring a claim before a competent court under Vietnamese law. Complaining to us does not limit your legal rights.

sections.heading: 14. Contact
body: Questions about these terms can be sent to Keemori's support email or Facebook Messenger.

meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: Keemori's privacy policy: the data we collect when designing event invitations to order, how we use it, who we share it with and your rights.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: This page explains what data we collect, what we use it for, who we share it with and what rights you have over your data.

sections.heading: 1. Scope
body: This policy applies to the Keemori website, our made-to-order event invitation design service, and the invitations created and shared through it.
For guest data in an invitation, the invitation owner decides what is collected; we process that data on the owner's behalf.

sections.heading: 2. Data we collect
body: Consultation details: your name, email, phone number, the channel you contact us on (Zalo, Facebook Messenger, email), a description of your event and your design brief.

Account data: the account we create using the email you provide, plus a display name and phone number if any. The initial password is set by us and sent to you; once you change it, your password is stored only as a one-way hash that we cannot read.

If you sign in with Google or Facebook, we receive your email address and display name from that provider, plus an identifier to recognise you next time. We never receive your password for those services.
Invitation content: the host name, event time and venue, photos, logos, invitation wording and gift details (if any) that you provide or enter yourself.
Content submitted by guests: names and wishes in the guestbook; and names, whether they will attend and how many people are coming if the invitation has an RSVP section.
Technical data: IP address, browser type, access time, and a random viewer ID stored in guests' cookies to count how many people have viewed an invitation.

Payment data: your orders (amount, voucher code used, time), plus the amount, time, and the sender's name and account number as reported to us by the bank through SePay for reconciliation. You pay from your own banking app using the VietQR code shown on the website; money goes straight into our bank account and we never receive or store your card number.

sections.heading: 3. How we use data
body: To advise you, design your invitation to order and keep in touch while we work on it.
To create, store and show your invitation to people who open its link.
To authenticate sign-ins, keep sessions and protect accounts from unauthorised access.
To create your payment order, match your bank transfer to it and send you a receipt.
To send transactional emails: account details, password resets and payment receipts. We do not send marketing email unless you sign up for it.
To count how many people have viewed an invitation, so you know how far it has reached.
To detect abuse, fight spam and improve the service.

sections.heading: 4. Cookies and similar technologies
body: We use cookies to keep you signed in and to refresh your session when it expires.

Guests who open an invitation get a cookie containing a random viewer ID. It is not linked to anyone's identity; it only ensures that one person opening the invitation several times is not counted as several people.
We use Google Analytics to measure traffic to our marketing and pricing pages. It sets analytics cookies and gives us aggregate figures — sessions, traffic sources, devices — not who you are.
Your invitation page is outside that measurement: we deliberately do not load Google Analytics on invitation pages, so invitation links and the information on them are not sent to Google.
No cookies are used for personalised advertising, and we do not use third-party ad tracking.
Some forms are protected by reCAPTCHA to block automated submissions; this means your browser exchanges data with Google under Google's own policy.

sections.heading: 5. Sharing and third parties
body: We do not sell your personal data.
Data is only shared with providers that help us run the service, and only to the extent each one needs:
- Our server and database hosting providers.
- Resend — sending transactional email (account details, password resets, payment receipts).
- SePay — notifying us of bank transactions so your bank transfer can be matched to your payment order automatically.
- Cloudflare R2 — storing and serving the photos on invitations.
- Google and Facebook — only if you choose to sign in with them.
- Google reCAPTCHA — blocking automated form submissions.
- Google Analytics — measuring traffic to marketing pages, not invitation pages.
- Photon / OpenStreetMap or Google Places — address suggestions when entering an event venue.
Messages you send us on Zalo or Facebook Messenger pass through those platforms and are subject to their own privacy policies.

Google Maps Embed runs in a guest's browser when an invitation includes a map. In that case the guest's browser connects directly to Google under Google's own policy, without going through our servers.
We may disclose data when lawfully required by a competent state authority.

sections.heading: 6. Public invitations, guestbook and RSVP
body: Anyone with an invitation link can see its content. Think carefully before including sensitive details such as a home address or personal bank account number.
Depending on the design, an invitation may have a guestbook — where guests leave their name and a wish — and an RSVP section, where guests say whether they will attend and how many people are coming.

Submitted wishes are held for approval and only appear on the invitation once the owner approves them. The owner can delete any wish. RSVP responses are never shown publicly; only the invitation owner can see them.
What guests enter belongs to the invitation owner; we store it on their behalf and use it for nothing else.

sections.heading: 7. Photos on invitations
body: Photos are recompressed before storage, and all metadata is removed in the process — including the GPS coordinates phones usually embed.
This is deliberate: an invitation is a public link, and a photo that still carries coordinates would reveal where it was taken to anyone who opens the invitation.
Uploaded photos are served from hard-to-guess links that do not require sign-in. Anyone with a photo's link can see it.
When an invitation is deleted, its photo files are deleted from storage, not just hidden from the interface.

sections.heading: 8. Security
body: Connections to the service are encrypted with HTTPS. Passwords are hashed one-way before storage.
Keemori staff see your invitation content while designing, revising and supporting it. Internal access to data is limited by role and used only for those purposes.
No system is perfectly secure; change your initial password, use a strong password and do not share your account.

sections.heading: 9. Your rights
body: You have the right to view, correct or request deletion of your personal data.
You have the right to request a copy of your data, including your history of accepting legal documents, and to withdraw consent you gave earlier.
To exercise these rights, send a request through the support channels on our Contact page; we may need to verify your identity first.

sections.heading: 10. Children
body: The person ordering a design and the account holder must be 18 or older. We do not knowingly collect children's data; if we find any, it will be deleted.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to this policy
body: This policy may be updated as the service or the law changes. The version and date of the latest update are always shown at the top of this page.

sections.heading: 12. Deleting your account
body: If you delete your account yourself under Account, your account data is permanently deleted, your email address is released and you can register again with it.
If we disable an account (for example, for breaching our terms), it loses sign-in access, related data is kept, and that email address cannot be registered again.
In both cases, orders and payment transactions are not deleted — accounting law requires us to keep these records.

sections.heading: 13. Retention
body: Paid invitations and their photos are kept for as long as your account exists; no automatic deletion applies to them.
Your account is kept for as long as you want to use it: we do not delete accounts for inactivity.
Orders and payment records are not deleted along with an invitation or account — see section 12.
Admin activity logs are kept for 24 months from the date recorded, then deleted automatically.

Database backups are kept for at most 30 days and then deleted. Because a backup is a snapshot of all data at one point in time, content you asked us to delete may still exist in backups that have not yet expired — no later than 30 days after you delete it, that content no longer exists anywhere in our systems. We do not use backups to restore data deleted at your request.

sections.heading: 14. Contact
body: Questions and requests to exercise your personal data rights can be sent to Keemori's support email or Facebook Messenger.

meta.title: Payment & Refund Policy
meta.description: How payment works for a made-to-order event invitation: pricing, 100% upfront payment, bank transfer, incorrect transfers and refunds.

paymentRefund.title: Payment & Refund Policy
paymentRefund.subtitle: This page explains how an invitation design order is quoted, paid and reconciled, and what happens when something goes wrong.

sections.heading: 1. Scope
body: This policy applies to every payment for Keemori's made-to-order event invitation design service (custom invitations).
This policy supplements our Terms of Service; where they conflict on payment matters, this page prevails.

sections.heading: 2. Prices
body: Prices are listed on the Pricing page, in Vietnamese đồng (VND), and include applicable taxes, if any. A package promotion and a voucher code (if you use one) are deducted directly from the amount you transfer and shown clearly on the payment screen before you confirm.
The price of an order is fixed when you press Pay and the order is created on the website. Later changes to our prices do not apply to orders already created.
You pay once per invitation: there is no subscription fee and no automatic renewal.
Custom invitations have no trial and no free plan.

sections.heading: 3. Payment upfront
body: You pay 100% of the order value before the invitation gets a public link. You can compose and preview it freely beforehand; the link is created only once the payment has reached our account.
Revisions within the brief agreed during the consultation cost nothing extra. Requests outside that brief may be quoted separately, and are only carried out with your agreement.

sections.heading: 4. Payment method
body: There is currently one payment method: bank transfer, made right on the website with a VietQR code. We do not accept credit cards and do not store any card details.

When you press Pay, the website creates an order and shows the amount, the receiving account details and the transfer reference, with a pre-filled VietQR code. The safest way to pay is to scan that code without changing anything.
If you transfer manually, keep the transfer reference exactly as given — it is how we tell which order an incoming payment belongs to.

When the money arrives, our automatic reconciliation through SePay (the service that reports bank transactions to us) matches it to your order and creates the invitation link, usually within seconds. You do not need to send us a screenshot of the transaction.

sections.heading: 5. Incorrect or short transfers
body: Wrong or missing transfer reference: the payment cannot be matched automatically and goes into a manual reconciliation queue. Contact support with the time of transfer and the amount, and we will match it for you.
Short payment: the order is recorded as underpaid and the invitation link is not created until you transfer the remaining amount.
Overpayment or duplicate transfer: the excess is not kept automatically. Contact support and it will be returned to you.
Every transfer into our account is recorded, including transfers not yet matched to an order — no payment goes missing.

sections.heading: 6. Receipts
body: Once we receive the money, we email a receipt with the amount received to the address on your account, and show a notice in the website's notification bell.
If you need a VAT invoice, please contact support with your invoicing details.

sections.heading: 7. Refunds
body: Each invitation is designed specifically for you and its link is created as soon as we receive payment, so payments are non-refundable.

The only exception is a technical fault caused by us: the invitation does not open, content displays incorrectly or is lost, or an agreed feature does not work. Send a complaint through our support channels and we will fix it as quickly as possible. If the fault is still not fixed more than 3 working days after we receive your complaint, we refund the full amount you paid for that invitation — you do not need to ask again.
Refunds are sent to the same bank account used for payment, within 7 working days of our decision to refund. If that account cannot receive the money, you can give us another account in your name.
Cases that are not refunded:
- Changing your mind or no longer wanting the invitation.
- The event being cancelled, postponed or rescheduled. If the time or venue changes, you can update those details yourself in your account.
- The design not meeting your aesthetic expectations.
- Incorrect content that you provided or entered.
- Not responding so that the invitation can be completed.
- Problems outside our system: your or your guests' connection, browser or device.
Overpayments and duplicate transfers are not covered by this section. Returning money we received in excess is not a refund, and it is always returned — see section 5.
A refund ends the transaction for that invitation: once refunded, you may no longer use the refunded invitation.
Publishing this process does not limit your rights under consumer protection law.

sections.heading: 8. Payment disputes
body: If you believe you were charged incorrectly, contact us before opening a dispute with your bank — we keep full transaction logs for reconciliation and can usually resolve it faster.
The formal complaint process is in the Complaints and dispute resolution section of our Terms of Service.

sections.heading: 9. Contact
body: Questions about payment, reconciliation or refunds can be sent to Keemori's support email or Facebook Messenger.

businessInfo.title: Business information
businessInfo.subtitle: Who is behind Keemori, what Keemori sells and how — what you should know before paying for an invitation.

owner.moitBadge: Registered with the Ministry of Industry and Trade

prices.caption: Listed price of the service
prices.itemNote: Paid once by bank transfer before design starts. The link is permanent with no viewer limit.

sections.heading: 1. Website owner
body: The Keemori website is owned and directly operated by the household business below to provide its own service. Keemori is not an e-commerce marketplace: we do not list goods or services from third parties, and every order on the website is a direct transaction between you and us.

sections.heading: 2. Our service
body: Keemori designs made-to-order online invitations for birthdays, openings, conferences, parties and other events: we build one invitation around your content and style, then deliver a link and QR code to send to your guests. Invitations open in the browser of any phone or computer; guests don't need to install an app or create an account.

An invitation is made of blocks you can switch on and off: event details, time and venue with a map, schedule, countdown and calendar, a note, a photo album, a gift box with bank-transfer QR codes, a guestbook, RSVP, personal guest links, a thank-you note and background music. Every feature is included in every invitation — there are no plans.

The website sells a single service: a custom-designed invitation at a fixed price per invitation, shown in the table below, paid once by bank transfer right on the website; the link is created when the money arrives. There is no trial. The link is permanent with no viewer limit.
Prices are listed in Vietnamese dong, include applicable taxes if any, and are paid once per invitation — no subscription and no automatic renewal.

sections.heading: 3. General terms of sale
body: These terms apply to every customer ordering a design on Keemori, individuals and businesses alike (shops, restaurants, event organisers…).
An order goes through four steps:
- Contact us by email, Zalo or Messenger: describe the event, the content and the style you want, then receive a quote.
- Pay the full order value by bank transfer (VietQR on the website) to the account in section 1. The invitation link is only created once the full amount has arrived.
- Keemori designs the invitation, creates a Keemori account for you and sends you the sign-in details so you can review the design.
- You approve the final version, the invitation is published and you receive the link and QR code to send to your guests.

We commit to: keeping invitation links working long-term with no viewer limit; answering every complaint within 3 business days at most; refunding the full price of an invitation that is faulty on our side and still not fixed after 3 business days.

You are responsible for: using only content and photos you have the right to use, not publishing content that breaks the law or infringes on others' rights, and checking your invitation carefully before sending the link to guests.

You accept the Terms of service and Privacy policy when you create an account. The full rights and obligations of both parties, along with the complaint and dispute process, are set out in the documents below.

sections.heading: 4. Delivery
body: Keemori is a digital service: there are no physical goods, no shipping and no delivery fees.

Your invitation is delivered as a link and a QR code, available under My invitations once you approve the final version. You send the link to guests yourself via Zalo, Messenger or text, or print the QR code on paper invitations.
Turnaround depends on how complex the design is and how quickly both sides reply; the expected date is given during the consultation.
If you have transferred the money but we have not started designing, contact us with the time and amount of the transfer — we will check it against the bank statement and confirm with you.

sections.heading: 5. Payment methods
body: Keemori accepts a single payment method: bank transfer, made right on the website with a VietQR code. We don't take cash, don't accept credit cards and never store your card details.

When you press Pay for an invitation, the website creates an order and shows the amount, the receiving account details (section 1) and the transfer reference. Scan the VietQR code, or keep the reference exactly as given if you transfer manually, so the system can recognise the payment.

Reconciliation is automatic through SePay: when the bank reports the credit, the money is matched to your order and the invitation link is created, usually within seconds. A transfer with the wrong reference is matched by hand when you contact us.
Payments go only to the account held in the name of the household business in section 1. If your banking app shows a different recipient name, don't transfer and let us know right away.

sections.heading: 6. Contact
body: Questions about the service, an order or anything on this page are handled through Keemori's support email, Zalo or Facebook Messenger. We reply within 3 business days at most.

notes.title: The lunar date on a Vietnamese invitation
paragraphs: Vietnamese invitations usually give the Gregorian date first and the lunar date in brackets. Older relatives check the lunar date, so getting a single number wrong is the first thing anyone notices.
The lunar year doesn't turn over with the Gregorian one. The Year of Đinh Mùi begins on 6 February 2027, so a wedding in January 2027 still falls in the Year of Bính Ngọ.
The tool uses the same astronomical algorithm and Vietnam time zone (UTC+7) that Keemori uses to print lunar dates on invitations, so the numbers here match the ones on your card.

faqs.question: How accurate is the conversion?
faqs.answer: It uses Hồ Ngọc Đức's algorithm in the Vietnam time zone (UTC+7), the common way the Vietnamese lunar calendar is computed today. For an important date, families may still double-check against a printed calendar.

faqs.question: Which lunar years are 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Most of 2026 is the Year of Bính Ngọ. The Year of Đinh Mùi starts at lunar new year, on 6 February 2027, so the days before it in early 2027 still belong to Bính Ngọ.

faqs.question: How is a leap month written?
faqs.answer: Add “nhuận” after the month, as in “tháng 6 nhuận”. 2025 has a leap sixth month; the tool detects it automatically when converting from a Gregorian date.

faqs.question: Does it tell me which days are auspicious?
faqs.answer: No. The tool only converts dates. Many families ask an elder or a date reader to choose the day — ask early, since you also need the venue to be free.

tables.title: Reception table calculator
tables.subtitle: Book too many and you pay for empty tables; too few and guests wait while extra ones are set up. A few numbers give you a reasoned estimate before you confirm with the venue.

widget.confirmedHint: Leave blank if nobody has replied yet. These guests are counted in full.

widget.rateHint: 80% is only a starting point to show the maths — adjust it to your family's and venue's experience.
widget.perTableHint: Ask about your exact hall: some seat 10, others 8 or 12.
widget.reserveHint: Ask the venue how unused spare tables are charged.
widget.note: This is an estimate. Ask the venue for its deadline for the final table count and its policy on late changes, then set your RSVP deadline before it.

howTo: Enter the total number of guests invited — count people, not invitations.
If you already have RSVPs, enter how many people are confirmed. The rest is estimated with your percentage.
Adjust seats per table and spare tables to match the venue, then read the number of tables to book.

notes.title: Getting the number close to reality
paragraphs: The surest way is real answers instead of guesses: ask guests whether they're coming and how many, then follow up individually with anyone who hasn't replied before the venue's deadline.
Attendance varies from wedding to wedding — distance, weekday versus weekend, and how the invitation was delivered all change it. That's why the tool lets you set the rate instead of assuming one.
On Keemori invitations, guests RSVP on the invitation itself and you see the summary in My invitations, so the “confirmed” box can hold real numbers.

faqs.question: How many people sit at a reception table?
faqs.answer: Ten per table is common, but some venues seat 8 or 12 depending on the hall and table style. Ask about your hall and enter it in “Seats per table”.

faqs.question: How many spare tables should I book?
faqs.answer: It depends on the venue's policy. Ask whether spare tables are only charged if used and when the final count is due, then set your spare tables accordingly.

faqs.question: What attendance rate is reasonable?
faqs.answer: There's no figure that fits every wedding. Use your family's experience as a starting point, and collect RSVPs as early as you can to replace the estimate with real numbers.

howTo: Open your online wedding invitation and copy its link.
Paste the link above. The QR code appears as soon as the link is valid.
Click “Download QR code (PNG)” to get a white-background image with margins, sharp enough to print.

notes.title: Printing the code on a paper invitation
paragraphs: A paper card is still the formal way to invite grandparents and elders. Add a small QR code on the back or a lower corner with a short line such as “Scan for the map and reception details”, and they get both.
Keep the code black on white with a white margin around it — pale or busy codes are hard for many phone cameras to read. Test on several phones before printing a large batch.
If your invitation is on Keemori, the “Get link & QR” box in My invitations already has a QR download button. This tool is for any other link, or when the link is all you have.

faqs.question: Does the QR code expire?
faqs.answer: No. The code contains only the link you entered, so it works for as long as the link opens. Keemori invitation links never change, and published invitations have permanent links.

faqs.question: Can I use it for links that aren't from Keemori?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any link starting with https:// or http:// works.

faqs.question: Is my link stored anywhere?
faqs.answer: No. The QR code is drawn in your browser; the link isn't sent to or stored on any server.

faqs.question: Where should the code go on a paper invitation?
faqs.answer: Usually on the back or a lower corner, with a line saying what scanning does. Avoid placing it over patterns or on a dark background.
